item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q018_tal_effector_repeat_lengths","answer":"SCOPe a.298.1.1 classifies the shared TAL-effector repeat architecture, not proteins by total chain length: a is the all-alpha class, a.298 is the TAL-effector repeat fold, a.298.1 the corresponding superfamily, and a.298.1.1 the TAL-effector family. d2kq5a_, d3v6pa_, and d4cj9a_ contain different numbers and/or construct extents of tandem TAL repeats, so their total lengths differ greatly. Their homologous approximately 34-residue repeat units nevertheless form the same characteristic two-helix modules and assemble into the same solenoidal superhelix. Sequence changes at the repeat-variable diresidue positions—including residues governing DNA-base recognition—do not negate that structural and evolutionary relationship. Thus the family assignment supports common ancestry and structural equivalence at the repeat-module level, but it does not imply identical DNA specificity, biological function, or full-length domain organization. For template selection, repeat count, construct boundaries, DNA-bound state, curvature, and RVD/register correspondence must be matched; raw length or family membership alone is insufficient.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
